subject: anatomy
subtopic: Lymphatic drainage — tracheobronchial nodes and bronchomediastinal trunks
prompt: Lymph from the lungs passes through tracheobronchial nodes. Efferent vessels ascending from these nodes contribute to which lymphatic trunks?
explanation: Tracheobronchial efferents ascend along the trachea and join vessels from other thoracic nodes to form the right and left bronchomediastinal trunks.

distractorExplanations.A: The named efferent trunks in this pulmonary pathway are bronchomediastinal, not jugular.
distractorExplanations.B: Lumbar trunks are not the thoracic efferent trunks formed by this lung drainage pathway.
distractorExplanations.D: Subclavian trunks are not the named continuation of tracheobronchial efferents in this pathway.

learningObjective: Trace lung lymphatic drainage from tracheobronchial nodes into bronchomediastinal trunks.

subject: anatomy
prompt: A lesion of a nerve formed from C3–C5 weakens contraction of the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm. Which nerve has been injured?
explanation: The diaphragm receives motor supply from the phrenic nerve, formed from C3–C5. Diaphragmatic contraction normally flattens its dome and increases thoracic volume.

distractorExplanations.B: The vagus is not the C3–C5 motor nerve supplying the diaphragm.
distractorExplanations.C: The recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies laryngeal muscles rather than the hemidiaphragm.
distractorExplanations.D: Intercostal nerves supply the thoracic wall; the diaphragm’s motor supply is phrenic.

learningObjective: Identify the phrenic nerve as the motor supply of the diaphragm.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Which statement best explains why examination of the posterior lower chest is important when assessing the inferior lobe of the right lung?

options.text: The right middle lobe covers nearly the entire posterior chest
The right superior lobe extends inferiorly over the whole diaphragmatic surface
The three right lung lobes have equal posterior surface areas
The costal surface of the inferior lobe lies against the posterior and inferior thoracic wall

explanation: The inferior lobe has a large costal surface against the posterior and inferior walls; the middle lobe lies mainly against the lower anterior and lateral wall.

distractorExplanations.A: The middle lobe is predominantly anterior and lateral, not the main lobe covering the posterior lower chest.
distractorExplanations.B: The superior lobe is mainly related to the upper anterolateral wall and apex, not the whole inferior surface.
distractorExplanations.C: The lobes have unequal surface relationships; the inferior lobe is particularly prominent posteriorly.

learningObjective: Relate the inferior pulmonary lobe to the posterior and inferior thoracic wall.

subject: anatomy
prompt: The suprapleural membrane supports the cervical pleura at the thoracic inlet. Which pair describes its principal bony attachments?

options.text: Clavicle and transverse process of C3
Medial margin of rib 1 and transverse process of C7
Medial margin of rib 12 and transverse process of C7
Xiphoid process and transverse process of T12

explanation: The suprapleural membrane attaches laterally to the medial first-rib margin and posteriorly to the C7 transverse process, supporting the cervical pleural dome.

distractorExplanations.A: The membrane is anchored to rib 1 and C7, not the clavicle and C3.
distractorExplanations.C: Rib 12 is at the inferior thorax and is not an attachment of this membrane over the lung apex.
distractorExplanations.D: These are inferior thoracic landmarks, not the attachments of the membrane at the superior thoracic aperture.

learningObjective: Identify the first-rib and C7 attachments of the suprapleural membrane.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers destined for glands of the nasal mucosa travel in the greater petrosal nerve. Where do these fibers synapse before postganglionic fibers accompany branches of V2?
explanation: Greater petrosal fibers from the facial nerve synapse in the pterygopalatine ganglion. Postganglionic fibers then accompany maxillary nerve branches to the glands.

distractorExplanations.B: The superior cervical ganglion is the synaptic site for the sympathetic pathway, not this parasympathetic pathway.
distractorExplanations.C: V2 branches distribute the postganglionic fibers, but the parasympathetic synapse is not in the trigeminal sensory ganglion.
distractorExplanations.D: The inferior vagal ganglion is not the relay for facial greater-petrosal secretomotor fibers to nasal glands.

learningObjective: Identify the pterygopalatine ganglion in the nasal secretomotor pathway.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Lymph from the posterior/main region of the nasal cavity follows the nasopharyngeal route. Which nodes are associated with this drainage?

options.text: Retropharyngeal and upper deep cervical nodes

explanation: Posterior nasal lymph drains toward retropharyngeal and upper deep cervical nodes. Anterior nasal lymph may pass forward onto the face toward submandibular nodes.

distractorExplanations.A: The submandibular pathway is associated with anterior nasal regions and does not describe the posterior route asked about.
distractorExplanations.B: Axillary nodes do not receive the principal posterior nasal drainage shown in these sources.
distractorExplanations.C: Tracheobronchial nodes are associated with pulmonary drainage, not the posterior nasal cavity.

learningObjective: Distinguish posterior nasal lymph drainage from the anterior facial route.

subject: anatomy
prompt: An artery ascends with the recurrent laryngeal nerve to enter the larynx deep to the inferior constrictor. The artery is the inferior laryngeal artery. From which artery does it arise?
explanation: The inferior laryngeal artery is a branch of the inferior thyroid artery, which arises from the thyrocervical trunk.

distractorExplanations.A: The superior thyroid artery gives rise to the superior laryngeal artery, not the inferior laryngeal artery.
distractorExplanations.C: The facial artery contributes to pharyngeal and tonsillar supply but is not the parent of the inferior laryngeal artery.
distractorExplanations.D: The ascending pharyngeal artery supplies the pharynx but is not the parent vessel specified here.

learningObjective: Identify the parent vessel of the inferior laryngeal artery.

subject: anatomy
prompt: Lymphatics from laryngeal mucosa above the vocal folds pass toward deep cervical nodes near the carotid bifurcation. Which artery do they accompany?
explanation: Lymphatics above the vocal folds follow the superior laryngeal artery to deep cervical nodes associated with the common carotid bifurcation.

distractorExplanations.A: The inferior laryngeal/inferior thyroid route is associated with drainage from below the vocal folds.
distractorExplanations.B: The lingual artery is not the artery followed by the supraglottic drainage pathway described here.
distractorExplanations.D: The superior labial artery is not part of this laryngeal lymphatic route.

learningObjective: Relate supraglottic lymph drainage to the superior laryngeal vascular route.
